name: tour
purpose: Product tour and onboarding: a sequence of steps, each anchored to an element of the page (or centered), with a spotlight that dims the page around the target, Next, Back, Skip, and Finish buttons, and progress such as '2 of 5'. Every step is a dialog (non-modal by default, modal on request); focus moves into the step and returns when the tour ends; a step whose target is missing is skipped with an event.
whenToUse: First-time guidance through a new screen or feature.
Explaining a changed layout after a release.
Walking through a multi-part workflow where each part is a visible control.
whenNotToUse: Information users need every time: put it in the interface or in help text.
A single hint next to one control: use Popover or Tooltip.
responsive: The panel is at most 24rem wide (narrower on small viewports), flips and shifts to stay in the viewport, and scrolls when taller than the available space; targets are scrolled into view.
rtl: Placements -start and -end follow the writing direction; ArrowRight and ArrowLeft are mirrored; the button row mirrors.
theme: Component tokens tour-bg, tour-radius, tour-shadow (panel), tour-backdrop (dimmed page), tour-spotlight-radius and tour-spotlight-ring (cut-out), tour-dot-color and tour-dot-active (progress dots). Text and progress pairs are in the contrast gate. Forced colors draw the spotlight as a Highlight outline, since shadows are not painted.
security: Titles and string content are set as text; Node content is inserted as given (the application owns it). Positions are set through the CSSOM, never as style attributes, so the component runs under a strict CSP.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry. Remembering that a user finished the tour is up to the application (listen to aui-finish and aui-skip).

performance.testedScale: Up to 30 steps per tour; one active tour per page.

limitations: One target per step; the spotlight is a rounded rectangle around it.
In modal mode the spotlighted element is shown but not interactive.
Targets inside closed shadow roots or other documents (iframes) cannot be found by selector; pass a function that returns the element.
unsupported: Steps that wait for the user to perform an action on the target (listen to the target yourself and call next()).
Rich text (HTML) strings as content: pass a Node.
antiPatterns: Long tours (more than about seven steps): split them by feature.
Starting a tour on every visit: store completion and start it once.
Pointing at elements that are not visible without explanation.
